mechanism_narrative: Persistently low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) indicate accommodative monetary policy that compresses equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate exceeding 9.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that anticipate economic contraction, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months when UNRATE > 9.5, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 215) signals unsustainable economic conditions requiring monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
